newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French December bond futures surged to a new contract high on a tide of bullish sentiment in international bond markets as fears of imminent U.S. interest rate rises ebbed.

Traders said the mood on Wednesday was overwhelming bullish, in contrast to the pessimism prevailing on Tuesday afternoon, although defensive positioning ahead of key U.S. jobs figures due on Friday could still erode some of today's gains.
The December contract has rallied four points in less than a month, shaving 44 basis points off the benchmark 10-year yield and bringing it closer the six percent target.

Traders said the catalyst for this morning's rally, in tandem with Bunds, was the strong performance of U.S. bonds overnight and that the move higher was amplified by short covering by those who were bearish on Tuesday.
The December contract opened at 125.20, opening up a gap above 125.10 and rallied as high as 125.44 were it ran into resistance before settling up 26 centimes at at 125.34.
One trader said the fact the market shrugged off talk of an early French general election, which a cabinet minister did not rule out, was indicative of the bullish tone on Wednesday.
"At other times we would have reacted badly, but today we had a market which was only going one way," he said.
Another trader said "at these levels I would advise my clients to be cautious, but I was doing that when the (future) was at 123.00."
Traders said it was a busy day in the cash market. One said domestic insurers were buyers of the long-end of the market and another said there was good two-way business all along the curve.
The 10-year spread over Bunds fluctuated between one and four basis points during the day to end unchanged at three.

There were few concerns about Thursday's OAT auction even with the bond market at the current high levels. The Treasury is due to sell between 16 and 18 billion francs of 2006, 2011 and TEC 10 OATs on Thursday morning.
One trader said market makers could try to drive the market down slightly on Thursday morning although the recent return of domestic investors to the long end would make the Treasury's job easier.
The franc climbed late in the session to a high of 3.3834 compared with a low of 3.3885 and 3.3870 late on Tuesday. December PIBOR settled at its contract high of 96.34.
